findings.title: One real signature on the first screen

findings.after: Lead with the screen only Consile has: for example a task list where each assignee shows today's attendance or leave status beside the work

findings.title: Refuse the default plan

findings.after: Merge the two security sections, drop the problem-solution pair, and order what remains by the buyer's question
findings.why: The stock order and repeated card grids make the page read as filled from a template despite the specific hero.
findings.fix: Keep the one move that serves the job; replace the others with a shape the client's material suggests.

findings.title: The accent marks action and state
findings.where: eyebrow pills, card icons and card links across the page, 1440, tiles/1440-02.png, tiles/1440-05.png, tiles/1440-07.png
findings.evidence: The palette table counts 34 uses of #f97015 at 1440: 30 text and 4 fills. Besides the "Start free" buttons, it colours the eyebrow pills "The solution", "Built for two journeys" and "FAQ", the icons on every feature and security card (key, document, webhook, cookie), the icon tiles on the journey cards and the card links "View list", "Privacy" and "Learn more".
findings.before: Orange on eyebrows, about 15 decorative icons and the card links as well as the buttons
findings.after: Orange kept for "Start free", "Book a demo" and the current state; eyebrows and icons in the ink or muted grey
findings.why: With orange on every card, the "Start free" button is one orange mark among dozens and stops standing out.
findings.fix: Remove the accent from decoration and labels; keep it on the action and the current state.

findings.before: Half of the hero h1 and one h2 word in the accent orange
findings.after: Headings in the ink #1d212b; the orange left to the "Start free" button beside them
findings.why: The 64px orange words outweigh the orange "Start free" button 230px below and compete for the first look.
findings.fix: Set display type in ink and keep the accent for the action under it.

findings.title: Glass only on navigation and controls
findings.where: section 5 card grid, 1440, tiles/1440-04.png and tiles/1440-05.png

findings.after: Opaque card fills; glass, if kept, only on the fixed header
findings.why: Blur on a flat ground does nothing visible and costs rendering on every scroll.
findings.fix: Make content panels opaque; keep glass, if the system wants it, on the nav bar.

findings.title: State colours keep their meaning
findings.where: "The problem" eyebrow and the numbers 1, 2 and 3 on the problem cards, 1440, tiles/1440-02.png

findings.after: The label and numbers in the muted grey; red kept for errors and destructive states
findings.why: Red here signals an error that is not there, and weakens the colour's meaning in the product's own forms.
findings.fix: Separate the accent hue from the state hues, or re-derive the state colours away from the accent.

findings.title: Heading formulas across the page
findings.where: h2s and h3s from 'The problem' to 'What we believe', 1440, tiles/1440-02.png to tiles/1440-06.png
findings.evidence: Failed T-HEADING-FORM: the page runs the problem/solution template ('Why teams struggle without Consile' with 'Fragmented tools create chaos. Here's what we fix.', then 'How Consile solves it'); the h3s are slogans with no naming noun ('Tool Overload', 'Flying Blind', 'Manual Busywork', 'One Platform, Zero Chaos', 'Workflows That Run Themselves', 'Running in Minutes, Not Months', 'Leave & Attendance on Autopilot'); the FAQ is 'Questions, answered' and the close is 'Ready to run tasks, people ops, and performance from one workspace?'.
findings.before: One Platform, Zero Chaos
findings.after: Head each card with the module and what it does: 'Leave requests approved in the app, balances updated automatically'; drop the problem/solution pair and lead with the modules.
findings.why: A reader scanning heads meets slogans before the modules that are the product's actual content.
findings.root: Problem/solution landing template with slogan h3s
findings.fix: Rewrite the heading as the section's claim in its own nouns: 'Rooms from £95, all with a garden view', not 'Meet our rooms'.

findings.title: Cadence devices past budget
findings.evidence: Failed T-CADENCE: the copy sheet counts a contrast frame ('Running in Minutes, Not Months') plus the 'not across four disconnected tools' and 'no glue code, no context loss' tails, 6 word triads ('people, tasks, and reporting', 'work, people, and performance', 'security, compliance, and operations'), and a closing quip in most cards ('One login, one dashboard.', 'no questions needed', 'Your policies are set.'). The sweep counts 17 dashes against a budget of 2; most join a list to a payoff ('Leave approvals, task notifications, attendance logs, EOD summaries — automated so your team can focus on actual work').
findings.before: See who's in, what's blocked, and how your team is performing — instantly, from any device, no questions needed.
findings.after: End each card on its fact; cut the payoff tails after the dash.
findings.why: The same list-dash-payoff beat in every card reads as one template voice and hides which claims are real.
findings.fix: Keep the strongest instance of each device and rewrite the rest as plain statements that end on information.

findings.title: Rhetorical questions in body copy
findings.evidence: Failed T-CADENCE: 'Who's present today? What's blocked? How much leave is left?' opens a card, and 'Still curious? Talk to us.' closes the FAQ intro. The FAQ questions themselves are not findings.
findings.before: Who's present today? What's blocked? How much leave is left?
findings.after: State the fact the dashboard gives: today's attendance, blocked tasks and leave balances on one screen.
findings.why: A run of three questions is a stock opener; the product mock beside it already answers them.
findings.fix: Answer the question in its place as a statement; end the sentence with a full stop.

findings.title: Labels that repeat their heading or change wording
findings.where: feature cards, security cards and actions, 1440
findings.evidence: Failed T-LABEL-READ: each feature card's link repeats the whole slogan head ('Explore Running in Minutes, Not Months', 'Explore Leave & Attendance on Autopilot'); the security cards use 'Learn more' six times; the demo is offered as 'Book a demo', 'Explore the live demo', 'Watch the demo' and 'Play Consile demo video', and /how-it-works is 'How It Works' and 'see how it works'.
findings.before: Explore Running in Minutes, Not Months
findings.after: Name the module in the link ('Leave and attendance'), and name each security link's page ('SAML SSO setup').
findings.why: Slogan-length link text is hard to scan, and six 'Learn more' links read as one in a link list.
findings.fix: Name the action and its object; pick one wording for the main action and use it at every placement.

findings.title: Lines that restate their heading

findings.after: Say it once in the hero; give the closing band the plan fact ('Free Starter plan for up to 5 people') and the button.
findings.why: Five restatements of one positioning line cost a 1,318-word page reading time without new information.
findings.fix: Delete the restating sentence and open the body with the first new fact; keep a repeated fact only where it decides something.

findings.title: Vary compositions
findings.fix: Change the composition of the middle section in each run of three; pick the shape the content suggests (a table for specifications, a showcase for one picture).

findings.where: "Enterprise-grade by default" (y=3742) and "Built with security & compliance at the core" (y=6089), tiles 1440-04 and 1440-07, 1440px
findings.evidence: Both sections list the same items: SSO and SCIM ("SAML 2.0 Single Sign-On", "SCIM 2.0 Provisioning" versus "SSO & SCIM provisioning"), audit logs ("Audit Log Streaming" versus "Audit-log streaming") and API ("Public API & Webhooks" versus "Signed webhooks & scoped API keys"). The enterprise grid also holds "Recurring Tasks" and "Cookie Consent", which are not enterprise features.
findings.before: Two security sections 2,300px apart, the first mixing in task and cookie features.
findings.after: Merge them into one security section and move "Recurring Tasks" to the feature grid.
findings.why: The visitor reads the same claims twice and meets a task feature under a security heading, so the section labels stop being reliable.
findings.title: One idea per section
findings.fix: Split the section, or cut the second idea to a line in the first.

findings.evidence: Ten of the eleven h1 and h2 elements are text-align center; only the hero h1 is left-aligned. The start-line count gives text on at least eight lines with 3 or more blocks (x=152, 168, 176, 196, 384, 560, 564, 932), because section containers change width (max-w-4xl, max-w-6xl) from section to section.
findings.before: A left-aligned hero over centred section heads in containers of changing width.
findings.after: Keep the hero's left edge at x=151 for the section heads, and use one container width for the card sections.
findings.why: The hero sets a left edge that no later section keeps, and the card grids start at 145, 169, 176 or 197 depending on the section.
findings.title: One alignment axis
findings.fix: Left-align the heading groups and body; keep centring for one short display line.

findings.title: One size per kind of element
findings.evidence: dom-1440.json gives the ten section h2s at six sizes: 44px ("Why teams struggle without Consile", "How Consile solves it"), 40px ("Built with security & compliance at the core"), 32px ("What we believe"), 28px ("Enterprise-grade by default"), 24px ("Choose your way in", "Questions, answered") and 20px (the closing CTA). The type table gives h3 card titles at 14, 15, 16, 12 and 20px. The sweep's type_ladder hit counts 23 distinct sizes, including half-pixel steps (9.5, 10.5, 11.5, 12.5).
findings.before: Section h2s at 20, 24, 28, 32, 40 and 44px; 23 sizes on the page
findings.after: One section-h2 size (for example 40px at 1440, 28px at 375), one card-title size, and a ladder of about 8 steps
findings.why: Section heads that change size from section to section tell the reader some sections matter more, when they are peers.
findings.root: per-section text-size utilities instead of a heading token
findings.fix: List the sizes per kind of element and collapse each kind to one step.

findings.title: Headings are set in one voice
findings.where: hero h1 (tiles/1440-00.png, 375-00.png) and h2 "Choose your way in", 1440 and 375
findings.evidence: The hero h1 "Everything your team runs on, in one workspace" sets "in one workspace" in brand orange at 69.6px (1440) and 41.6px (375). The type table also lists "your" in the h2 "Choose your way in" set apart by colour at 24px. Two headings carry an accent-coloured phrase.
findings.before: "Everything your team runs on, **in one workspace**" with the last phrase in orange
findings.after: Each heading in one colour; let the hero's size and weight carry it
findings.why: Recolouring the payoff phrase is the stock generated hero, and repeating it on a later h2 turns it into a habit rather than a signature.
findings.fix: Set the heading in one weight, one style and one colour; move the stress to a line break.

findings.title: Each face has one job
findings.evidence: fonts.json at 1440 shows Outfit drawing only the 8 word spans of the hero h1 (39 characters at 69.6px). Figtree draws every other heading, including the 44px section h2s, and all text (248 elements). The two faces are both geometric sans with similar proportions, so the switch reads as a slight inconsistency rather than a contrast.
findings.before: Outfit for one heading, Figtree for every other heading and all text
findings.after: Figtree for the hero too, or Outfit for every display heading (h1 and h2)
findings.why: A second face used once, and close to the first, adds a family without adding a role.
findings.fix: Give each face one role and move stray elements onto it; drop a face that has no role of its own.

findings.title: The scale fits the medium
findings.evidence: The type table gives body at a 14px median (38 of 42 paragraphs) and h3 card titles at a 14px median, so the h3/body step is 1.00x; the sweep's flat_hierarchy hit reports the same. Card titles such as "Tool Overload" and "Workspace isolation" differ from their descriptions only by weight 500 against 400 and a darker grey.
findings.before: Card titles and body both at 14px, separated by one weight step
findings.after: 16px body on this marketing page (C12) with card titles at about 18 to 20px
findings.why: On a landing page read once, 14px body with same-size titles makes every card read as one grey block.
findings.fix: Pick the medium's ratio, give each role a step, and collapse the sizes between steps.

findings.title: Small labels earn their caps
findings.evidence: The type table counts 18 small uppercase tracked labels at 1440. Most sit inside the product preview ("TASKS DUE", "ATTENDANCE", 10px at 0.1em) and belong to that illustration. On the page itself, "OUR VALUES" sits in tracked orange caps above "What we believe", while the other section labels ("The problem", "The solution", "Trust & security") are sentence-case pills.
findings.before: OUR VALUES in tracked caps, other section labels in sentence case
findings.after: One label style for every section label, sentence case
findings.why: One label in a different setting from its peers looks like a leftover from another template.
findings.fix: Set labels in the body face a step smaller, in sentence case, untracked.

findings.evidence: focus indicator visible but faint: 2.68:1 against the unfocused state (target 3.0:1, WCAG 2.4.13)
findings.title: Visible focus everywhere
findings.fix: Use :focus-visible with a 2px ring offset 2px in a contrasting colour.

findings.title: Every headline promise is pictured
findings.evidence: T-PROMISE-PICTURED fails. 'Shifts, Rotations & Swap Requests', 'Guided Onboarding for New Hires' and 'KPI Reviews & Performance Tracking' each make a concrete promise and are pictured only by a small orange line icon.
findings.before: Line icons for concrete modules
findings.after: One product screenshot for each of the three modules that carry the idea (shifts, leave, reviews)
findings.why: A buyer comparing HR tools needs to see the shift swap or the review screen, and the page shows an icon instead.
findings.fix: Add the picture that proves the line, or rewrite the line to what the page can show.

findings.title: A card has a border or a shadow
findings.where: review-site tiles, problem cards, feature cards, stats bar and FAQ rows, 1440, tiles/1440-02.png to tiles/1440-07.png
findings.evidence: The palette table counts 60 elements with both a border and a shadow; 58 share the recipe rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.06) 0 1px 3px plus rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.04) 0 4px 16px, and the sweep's card_kit hit counts 83 containers with that shadow. The table also lists 6 shadow recipes, including an orange glow rgba(249, 112, 21, 0.45) on the hero button and a heavy rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.25) 0 25px 50px on the video play button.
findings.before: Hairline border plus a two-layer shadow on every card, and 6 shadow recipes in all
findings.after: One edge per card (the hairline on the #f8f8f6 page) and one resting shadow reserved for the product preview
findings.why: When every card floats, the product preview loses the one lift that should single it out.
findings.fix: Keep the border on flat surfaces and the shadow on floating ones; drop the other.

findings.where: features and enterprise sections, tiles 1440-03 to 1440-05, 1440px
findings.evidence: The sweep reports 213 words on screen 4 (words_per_screen) and 1,318 words on the page (page_words, budget 675). The enterprise grid alone holds ten cards, each with a heading, a two-line paragraph and a "Learn more" link.
findings.before: Persuade page carrying feature-reference density.
findings.after: Move the 24-feature and enterprise detail to the features page that "View all 24 features" already links to, and keep the top three on the home page.
findings.why: A visitor deciding whether to try the tool meets a reference list; the density belongs to a features page, not to the home page.
findings.title: Density fits the job
findings.fix: Move the spacing scale to the job's step and apply it evenly.
